messages.author: 7dd668eb41c5bfd9
messages.subject: Error upgrading PyStan to 2.6
parts:
Hey all,

I'm running OS X Yosemite 10.10.2. I've tried to upgrade my PyStan install from 2.5.0 to 2.6.0 and I keep getting this error message:

Warning: Can't read registry to find the necessary compiler setting


Make sure that Python modules _winreg, win32api or win32con are installed.


This happens regardless of whether I use pip or compile from source. Looks like the installer is searching for some Windows-specific files. Has anyone else encountered this problem and/or found a solution?


I've attached the full install log as a text file.


Thanks!


Nathan

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error upgrading PyStan to 2.6
parts:
Hi Nathan,

I'd recommend deleting all trace of the previous PyStan and trying
again. Perhaps you can see if there's a pystan directory underneath

`/opt/local/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/2.7/lib/python2.7/`?

I'm not sure what's causing the error (or the strange warning).

Keep us posted. Feel free to open an issue on github,
https://github.com/stan-dev/pystan

Best wishes,

-ar

If you just want to use Stan from Python, there's other two ways.
pyRserve let Python controls Stan through R.
Another solution is my codes: https://github.com/t3476/Python-Kits-CmdStan, which use cmdstan rather than linking stan directly
It looks PyStan still causes problems.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error upgrading PyStan to 2.6
parts:
Hi He-chien Tsai,

Allen helped me fixed my problems with Pystan already. I was using an (extremely) old version of pip (v1.4) to update Pystan. Looks like theres a minimum version requirement of pip for the most recent Pystan install to work. Not surprising, considering the new version is around v6.5 or so. I was just way behind.

Nate

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error upgrading PyStan to 2.6
parts:
There tend to be issues in just about any software
with enough people banging on it! What looks bug free
for the developer in their intended usage looks
rathe different when 1000 people start using it in
all sorts of unanticipated ways (or just hitting more
edge/corner cases).

At the same time, there is something to be said
for simplifying the interfaces, and we're working in
that direction.

I'm still not sure if we should stop trying to wrap
at the C++ level and just wrap up a Stan process. More
at a future Stan meeting (I'll definitely give you a heads
up if we plan to discuss, Allen).

- Bob
